answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a refundable bond before its bids enter a scarce-work auction. The protocol releases the bond after verified delivery and slashes it when linked accounts coordinate to claim the same task; for example, jobs tagged nectar, juniper, or willow still draw on one shared bond rule. Each fake account ties up capital for the auction period and risks losing its full bond, so creating a thousand Sybils costs a thousand deposits plus the opportunity cost of locked funds, rather than being free.
